references.text: Abraham also named a place after the Lord (JHVH Jireh - The Lord sees), in the same way that Moses called the altar 'The Lord is my banner'.
Jacob built an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel, parallel to how Moses built an altar and gave it a name that honored God.
Jacob built an altar at Bethel, a practice that Moses continues by building altars to remember God's intervention.
The context for the altar-building: the victory over Amalek led Moses to call the altar 'The Lord is my banner'.
Moses built an altar at Mount Sinai, showing his practice of building altars to mark important events with God.
Gideon built an altar and called it 'The Lord is peace' (JHVH Shalom), in the same way that Moses gave the altar a name describing the Lord's character.
Isaiah speaks of a banner (נֵס) that God gives to those who fear him, linking to the concept of the Lord as a banner.
The shoot from Jesse's root shall stand as a banner (נֵס) for the peoples, a messianic prophecy connecting to the Lord as a banner.
The psalmist asks to be able to lift up the banner in the name of the Lord, reflecting the theme of the Lord as the banner of victory.
